title: Generate the release notes from git, not from memory
summary: Build a changelog straight out of the commit range since the last tag, grouped by Conventional Commit type, with ticket references — the whole pipeline in a handful of commands.
mental_model: A changelog is a formatted `git log` over one range. Everything hard about it — which commits, which order, which fields — is a range and a format string. Nothing needs to be remembered or maintained by hand.

setup.run: git commit -q -m "feat(dosing): add calibrated dose calculation" --trailer "Refs: ABH-101"
git commit -q -m "fix(pump): stop stalling below 900 RPM" --trailer "Refs: ABH-204"
git commit -q -m "docs: document the alert thresholds"
git commit -q -a -m "fix(dosing): reject non-positive doses" --trailer "Refs: ABH-233"

steps.title: Find the previous release automatically
steps.why: `describe --tags --abbrev=0` prints the nearest tag with no suffix — the last release, discovered rather than hardcoded. This is the first line of every changelog script.
steps.expect: v1.0.0, found without anyone typing it.

verify.label: the previous release tag is discoverable

steps.title: List what has shipped since
steps.why: `<tag>..HEAD` with `--no-merges` gives the human-written commits and drops the merge noise. That range is the entire scope of the release.
steps.expect: Five commits — two features, two fixes, one docs change.

verify.label: the release range is five commits

steps.title: Format them as release notes
steps.why: A pretty format turns the log into markdown directly. `%s` is the subject and `%h` the sha — enough for a usable changelog in one command.
steps.expect: A bulleted list you could paste into a release.

steps.title: Group by Conventional Commit type
steps.why: Because the subjects follow a convention, grepping by prefix produces sections. This is all that changelog generators do — the convention is what makes it possible, not the tool.
commands: sh -c 'range=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD; for t in feat fix docs; do echo; echo "### $t"; git log --no-merges --pretty=format:"- %s" $range | grep "^- $t" || echo "- none"; done'
steps.expect: Three sections, populated from the commit messages.

steps.title: Pull the ticket references out
steps.why: `%(trailers:key=Refs,valueonly)` extracts the structured field. Now the release notes link to tickets without anyone maintaining a mapping by hand.
steps.expect: Each entry annotated with its ticket, and a de-duplicated list of every ticket in the release.

steps.title: Write the changelog file
steps.why: Generate it into CHANGELOG.md and commit it as part of the release. Because it is generated, it can never drift from what actually shipped.

actions.run: sh -c 'range=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD; { echo "# Changelog"; echo; echo "## v1.1.0"; echo; for t in feat fix docs chore; do lines=$(git log --no-merges --pretty=format:"- %s [%(trailers:key=Refs,valueonly)]" $range | grep "^- $t"); [ -n "$lines" ] || continue; case $t in feat) echo "### Features";; fix) echo "### Fixes";; docs) echo "### Documentation";; *) echo "### Other";; esac; echo "$lines"; echo; done; } > CHANGELOG.md'

verify.label: the changelog is generated from the commit range
verify.hint: git log <last-tag>..HEAD with a pretty format

steps.title: Tag the release and verify the notes match
steps.why: Tag after generating, so the changelog commit is inside the release. Then `git log v1.0.0..v1.1.0` should list exactly what the changelog claims — a check worth building into CI.
steps.expect: Two feat commits, matching the Features section.

verify.label: the release is tagged at the changelog commit
the range contains exactly the two features the changelog lists
a grouped changelog with ticket references was generated from git
verify.hint: git log <last-tag>..HEAD, grouped by Conventional Commit prefix

verify.label: the generated changelog is committed with the release

pitfalls: `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` returns the nearest tag on the current branch. On a release branch that is what you want; on a feature branch it may surprise you.
Squash-merging rewrites subjects, so a Conventional Commit prefix set on the branch may not survive to main. Enforce the format on the merge commit too.
Shallow CI clones cannot see the previous tag. `fetch-depth: 0` in your workflow, or describe fails and the changelog comes out empty.
Generate the changelog BEFORE tagging, so the changelog commit is part of the release it describes.
A commit-msg hook enforcing the convention is what makes all of this reliable. Without it the grouping quietly loses commits.
